findings.title: New abstract getShortcut() breaks existing custom grants
findings.body: File adds abstract String getShortcut() to OAuth2GrantTypeFactory with no default. Any existing third-party OAuth2GrantTypeFactory implementation compiled against the old interface will fail at runtime with AbstractMethodError / NoSuchMethodError when DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory calls gtf.getShortcut(), and will fail to compile on upgrade. A new SPI method must have a default implementation (e.g. default return "na") to remain backward compatible.

findings.title: Removed public copy constructor Context(Context)
findings.body: The diff deletes the public Context(Context context) copy constructor. External grant implementations or extensions that copied the context will no longer compile, and even if recompiled the grantType field would not be copied. The constructor should be retained (deprecated if desired) and updated to copy the new grantType field.

findings.title: NPE when formParams is null or missing grant_type
findings.body: In OAuth2GrantType.Context constructor, code does formParams.getFirst(OAuth2Constants.GRANT_TYPE) with no null check on formParams. Callers that construct a Context with null formParams will get NullPointerException during token request handling. Must null-check formParams before reading grant_type.

findings.title: Copy-paste null check validates grantType twice, never rawTokenId
findings.body: Constructor does Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null grantType not allowed"); followed by Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed");. The second check should validate rawTokenId, so a null rawTokenId is never rejected and later causes NullPointerException in encodeTokenId when concatenating ':' + rawTokenId, with a confusing failure.

findings.title: Token issuance fails hard on unknown grant type
findings.body: encodeTokenId() throws IllegalStateException when factory.getShortcutByGrantType() returns null for an unrecognized grantType. TokenManager.initToken() calls this unconditionally for every access token with no try/catch or fallback to raw UUID. Any custom grant, ad-hoc ClientSessionContext, or future grant not in the maps turns a token request into a 500 error. Encoding must fall back to the UNKNOWN "na" shortcut instead of throwing.

findings.title: Decoder throws on malformed/legacy token IDs
findings.body: getTokenContextFromTokenId() throws IllegalArgumentException when the prefix before ':' is not exactly 6 chars or contains unknown shortcuts. Old UUID-only tokens are handled only when there is no colon; any legacy or foreign ID that happens to contain a colon, or a truncated/corrupt ID, will throw and, once callers use this for introspection/userinfo/session lookup, will cause request failures instead of gracefully returning UNKNOWN context. Should return UNKNOWN context for unparseable IDs.

findings.title: Unchecked cast breaks startup with custom grant factories
findings.body: postInit() and getGrantTypeByShortcut() blindly cast every OAuth2GrantType provider factory to OAuth2GrantTypeFactory. If a deployment provides a custom OAuth2GrantType factory that does not implement the new sub-interface (possible before this API change), server startup throws ClassCastException and the whole server fails to boot. Must use instanceof filtering or defensive handling.

findings.title: isAccessTokenId matcher inverted and uses wrong offsets
findings.body: Matcher does if (items[0].substring(3,5).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false; which returns false exactly when the grant matches (inverted logic, should be !equals). It also extracts substring(3,5) while the 6-char prefix is session(0-1)+token(2-3)+grant(4-5), so grant is at substring(4,6). The helper will reject correct token IDs and accept wrong ones, and can throw StringIndexOutOfBoundsException on short prefixes without a length check.
